### Contributions
- Analyzes learning noisy archetypes in the exponential Hopfield network, whose zero-temperature update is softmax attention over examples.

- Identifies memorization as a random-energy-model freezing transition and links it to softmax concentration on the nearest training example.

# Stateful Testing for Deep Learning Compilers

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/10/2610.22003.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Identifies compiler state retained across invocations as a source of bugs missed by isolated tests.
- Models tests as a program plus an invocation sequence, then mutates sequences to explore stateful behavior.
- Uses a three-way differential oracle: uncompiled execution, compiled execution with reset state, and compiled execution with retained state.
- Replays suspected failures under controlled state conditions and shortens invocation sequences while preserving the bug.

### Method
Rondo combines invocation-sequence mutation with an MCMC sampler guided by compilation

candidates.snippet:
Introduction
The evolution of large-scale recommendation models has largely been a history of architectural innovation: from early feature-crossing and shallow models such as LR, FM and FFM (McMahan et al., 2013; Rendle, 2010; Juan et al., 2016), to deep architectures with explicit memory and cross networks such as Wide & Deep, DeepFM, and DCN (Cheng et al., 2016; Guo et al., 2017; Wang et al., 2017), to user-behavior sequence modeling such as DIN, DIEN, and SIM (Zhou et al., 2018, 2019; Pi et al., 2020), and more recently to ranking backbones that introduce Transformer-attention mechanisms and tokenized interactions, such as RankMixer, TokenMixer-Large, and MixFormer-style interaction model

# MAI-Gym: An Open All-in-One Platform for GUI Agent Evaluation and RL Training across Mobile and Computer Environments

## Archive
path: inbox/2026/10/783af372cb.html

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduces MAI-Gym, an open platform unifying GUI agent evaluation, data collection, and online RL training across mobile, computer, and web environments.
- Provides a shared rollout pipeline supporting ten benchmarks and up to 20,000 parallel environment instances.
- Enables synthesis of resettable mocked applications and coherent cross-app tasks with execution-validated verifiers.
- Releases the framework, synthesis skills, mocked apps, 2,000 verified tasks, and a 9B agent checkpoint.

- Grounds drafts with read-only tool calls and defers the first environment-modifying action.
- Uses one parallel prefill pass to accept the longest semantically valid prefix and repair the first rejected step.

### Method

# Kronecker Delta Rule for Long Context Linear Attention

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/10/2610.26834.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduces the Kronecker Delta Rule for targeted, minimally invasive updates to associative matrix memories.
- Presents KronLSTM, integrating the rule into linear attention for long-context language modeling.
- Analyzes memory dynamics as a Markov chain converging to a steady-state distribution, with uniformly bounded expected memory norm.

### Method
KronLSTM revises targeted associations by changing memory along a single direction in matrix space, reducing interference without additional memory-state normalization or stabilization.

# Kronecker Delta Rule for Long Context Linear Attention

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/10/2610.26834.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduces the Kronecker Delta Rule for targeted, minimally invasive revision of associative matrix memories.
- Develops KronLSTM, a linear-attention architecture that integrates this rule into the xLSTM family.
- Shows theoretically that memory dynamics converge to a steady-state distribution and maintain a uniformly bounded expected memory norm.

### Method
Design a single-direction matrix-space memory update that corrects targeted associations, then analyze its recurrent dynamics as a Markov chain and evaluate KronLSTM against linear-attention baselines.
focus.title: Kronecker Delta Rule for Long Context Linear Attention

The bidirectional memory uses a hidden dimension of 512. Visual keys project V-JEPA 2 features from 1408 to 512 dimensions, while visual and action values are modeled by 2-layer stateful Mamba encoders with state dimension 16. 3.2 Observation-Guided Video-Context Routing
Asynchronous execution reuses one planner video context for multiple action chunks, which amortizes video-DiT computation but creates a context-alignment problem: before the next planner refresh, the robot state and visual scene may have changed. Observation-Guided Video-Context Routing (OVCR) addresses this by using the latest visual observation to convert the shared planner context into a chunk-specific context. Instead of feeding dense visual tokens into the high-frequency action DiT, OVCR compresses them into a small set of routing queries that select and edit the relevant planner context before action denoising. # UniWALM: Unified World Action Language Model for Embodied Robot Control

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/10/2610.28626.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Unifies video, action, and language learning in one shared representation for robot control.
- Generates textual memory and actions synchronously, enabling a language-as-memory loop without a separate planner or memory bank.
- Introduces Flow Matching with Correction (FMC) to improve recovery from perturbed action trajectories at no inference-time cost.

### Method
A mixture-of-transformers backbone with modality-specific diffusion heads that co-denoise video, action, and language; generated language is re-consumed at the next step.
